claims.statement: Open SWE's backend is a LangGraph application that serves multiple graphs (agent, reviewer, analyzer, chat, scheduler) together with a FastAPI app (agent.webapp:app), all wired through langgraph.json which also declares the checkpointer TTL policy and .env env file.

make dev runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024`, serving all graphs plus the FastAPI app on http://localhost:2024 so that both the /webhooks/* and /dashboard/api/* endpoints are available from one process.

make run runs `uvicorn agent.webapp:app --reload --port 8000` and serves the FastAPI app without the LangGraph runtime, which is insufficient for the dashboard's Agents chat features that call LangGraph; full local dev therefore requires make dev on :2024.

make install installs backend dependencies including dev extras via `uv sync --extra dev`, and the Makefile exposes uv-run wrappers for pytest (test/integration_tests), ruff (lint/format/format-check), and ty (typecheck) over agent and tests.

The local dev server is constrained to langgraph-api >=0.13.3,<0.14 in pyproject.toml to match langgraph.json's 0.13.3 manifest and avoid uv resolving the end-of-life 0.10.3 runtime; the standalone Docker image uses the matching 0.13.3 API release.

langgraph.desktop.json is a separate trimmed deployment manifest for the desktop build that exposes only the agent graph, disables the built-in UI, and configures a local auth handler (agent.local_auth:auth) with Studio auth disabled.
The dashboard is part of a pnpm workspace whose members are ui, desktop, and tests/e2e, and Turborepo orchestrates the per-package dev, build, typecheck, test, and check tasks.

make web runs `turbo run dev --filter=open-swe-dashboard`, starting the dashboard Vite dev server on http://localhost:3000, which proxies backend-owned paths to DASHBOARD_API_URL (defaulting to http://localhost:2024) so no ui/.env is needed and one build can front any backend.

The dashboard build/typecheck/test scripts fan out across the workspace through Turborepo, while lint (oxlint) and format/format:check (oxfmt) run once from the repo root over all JS/TS files and are not Turborepo tasks.

Turborepo's build task caches .output/**, .vercel/output/**, and build/**, and treats DASHBOARD_API_URL, VERCEL, E2E_HARNESS, and any VITE_* variable as cache-affecting build inputs so changing them invalidates cached builds.

The Electron desktop app in desktop/ bundles the compiled dashboard UI, is run in development with make desktop (pnpm run dev:desktop) against a running backend, and is packaged with `pnpm --dir desktop run pack` (unpacked) or `pnpm --dir desktop run dist` (installer); packaged builds prompt for the backend URL on first launch rather than defaulting to any hosted deployment.

make install-desktop installs or updates Open SWE Desktop on macOS by refusing to run with a dirty working tree, fast-forwarding to main, then invoking scripts/install_desktop.sh, whereas make install-checkout runs that script against the current checkout without touching git state.

scripts/install_desktop.sh is macOS-only, verifies node, ditto, uv, and a pnpm/corepack launcher are present, packs the desktop app, and atomically swaps it into /Applications (or ~/Applications when /Applications is not writable).
scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py builds a LangSmith sandbox snapshot from a Docker image using SandboxClient and prints the resulting UUID to set as DEFAULT_SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID.

scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py is a one-time backfill that deletes expired one-shot thread_wakeup crons from a deployment, resolving the deployment URL from --url/LANGGRAPH_URL/LANGGRAPH_URL_PROD and the API key from LANGGRAPH_API_KEY/LANGSMITH_API_KEY/LANGSMITH_API_KEY_PROD.

examples/github-actions/set-base-snapshot.yml is a copy-ready reference workflow that rolls a new base sandbox snapshot out to a running deployment from CI by PUTting to /dashboard/api/sandbox-settings, authenticating with GitHub Actions OIDC (id-token: write) so no long-lived secret is stored.

Admin-gated sandbox-settings CI access is allowlisted via ADMIN_OIDC_SUBJECTS (matched against the OIDC token's sub/repository claim) with an ADMIN_OIDC_AUDIENCE defaulting to open-swe, or alternatively an admin personal access token whose owner is listed in CONFIGURED_ADMINS; secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN works for neither because installation tokens have no user identity and are not OIDC tokens.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone production LangGraph API server image (not the sandbox image) from langchain/langgraph-api:0.13.3-py3.14, installing the repository with uv and baking the five graph registrations, HTTP app (agent.webapp:app), and checkpointer TTL into LANGSERVE_GRAPHS, LANGGRAPH_HTTP, and LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINTER; it exposes port 8000.

A standalone backend container requires the Agent Server backing services and settings — DATABASE_URI (Postgres), REDIS_URI (Redis), LANGSMITH_API_KEY, and LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY — plus LANGGRAPH_URL set to the public backend URL, and must not use scale-to-zero hosting because background runs rely on Redis/Postgres-backed workers staying available.

ui/Dockerfile is a multi-stage Node 24 build (run from the repo root) that installs the workspace with the frozen pnpm lockfile, builds open-swe-dashboard into a Nitro .output server, runs it on port 8080, and reads the backend it fronts from DASHBOARD_API_URL at runtime so one image serves any deployment.

In production the dashboard proxies browser /dashboard/api/* requests and /webhooks/* deliveries to the backend and forwards the osw_session cookie on server renders, making requests same-origin when DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL and the GitHub App callback are set to the dashboard origin; a cross-origin alternative points the browser at the backend via VITE_DASHBOARD_API_BASE_URL and requires the dashboard origin in DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

The backend can alternatively be deployed to LangGraph Cloud / Platform by connecting the repository and setting the same environment variables, using the hosted deployment URL for LANGGRAPH_URL and webhook callbacks.

The production Nitro proxy requires DASHBOARD_API_URL at request time and throws if it is unset, rather than falling back to a backend; it proxies the original path and query while preserving OAuth redirects manually.

The FastAPI app rejects a wildcard DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configuration because credentials are enabled, and applies the configured origins to credentialed CORS with dashboard, plan, workflow, webhook, and health routers installed.

FastAPI startup pins one event loop, validates sandbox and local-development LLM configuration before serving, and closes cached models on shutdown; its `GET /health` endpoint returns `{"status": "healthy"}`.

The dashboard's development proxy covers additional mock-harness and raw LangGraph paths, but a normal production Nitro build registers its proxy handler only for `/dashboard/api/**` and `/webhooks/**`.

The desktop client runs a private loopback LangGraph service for local tasks, proxies its bundled UI's dashboard API calls to the selected backend, and stops the local service with the Electron application.
The production backend must protect publicly reachable built-in LangGraph API routes with private networking, a gateway, or custom authentication when `LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop` is used.
The UI Vercel configuration builds with `pnpm run build`, installs the dashboard workspace from the frozen lockfile, and enables Git deployment only for main, preview, and prod branches.
